description: This binary search tree has four levels and 15 nodes with values 1 through 15. All edge arrows point from parent to child. The root at the first level is 8, with left child 4 and right child 12.

On the second level, node 4 has left child 2 and right child 6, and 12 has left child 10 and right child 14. Nodes at the third level point to the eight leaves on the fourth. The left and right children of 2 are 1 and 3, those of 6 are 5 and 7, those of 10 are 9 and 11, and those of 14 are 13 and 15.

frames.explanation: The ordering of the binary search tree recurs in each subtree. At root 8, the left subtree contains 1 through 7, all smaller than 8, and the right subtree contains 9 through 15, all larger than 8. The same rule applies farther down. For example, the left subtree of 4 contains 1 through 3, all smaller than 4. Its right subtree contains 5 through 7, all larger than 4 and smaller than root 8.
frames.title: Binary search tree containing 1 through 15

summary: At every node of a binary search tree, all values in the left subtree must be smaller than the node's value and all values in the right subtree must be larger.
title: Binary search tree containing 1 through 15
